title: Math Functions
story: Your friend is struggling with algebra homework. You decide to build a pocket calculator of reusable math functions so they can check their answers instantly!
why: Mathematical operations are the most natural use of functions — one input in, one output out. They're perfect for practicing function design.
analogy: Math functions are like a Swiss Army knife of numbers — each blade does one specific cut, but together they handle any job.
try_it: Add an `is_multiple_of` function that checks if one number is divisible by another (hint: use `%`). Then test `is_multiple_of(15, 5)` — should be true.
tips: Functions that return `Bool` should be named like questions: `is_even`, `is_positive`
Each math function should do ONE operation — square, cube, absolute — not everything at once
common_mistakes: Using `=` instead of `==` for comparison: `if n = 0` is wrong; use `if n == 0`
Forgetting `return` in an `if/else` — both branches must return a value
Writing `-n` when n is positive thinking it'll work — `-(-5)` correctly gives `5`, but double-check your logic
